book.title: Thoracic Serious Pathology and Visceral Referred Pain
book.lead: When the thoracic spine is the messenger, not the source.

blocks.text: Internal organs share nerve pathways with the thoracic spine segments. Pain from an organ can therefore be felt in the back or chest wall. This is called visceral referred pain. Knowing the common referral areas helps you recognise a pattern that does not fit a mechanical problem.

rows: Central chest, left arm, jaw, between the shoulder blades
Between the shoulder blades, tearing, through to the chest or abdomen
Chest wall, shoulder tip (diaphragm), worse on breathing
Behind the sternum, mid-back, related to swallowing
Upper abdomen, mid-thoracic (around T6 to T10), related to meals
Right upper abdomen, right shoulder blade
Upper abdomen boring through to the back, eased by leaning forward
Loin (T10 to L1), groin, with urinary symptoms or fever

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Thoracic pain with leg weakness or bladder change
Cancer history with new thoracic pain
Same-week medical review, sooner if neurological signs

steps: **Does movement change the pain?** No: think visceral or serious pathology.
**Vital signs abnormal or systemic features?** Medical review at the correct urgency.
**Neurological signs in the legs?** Urgent or emergency referral.
**All clear:** proceed with the mechanical thoracic pathway (Vol 3 Ch 1).

sections.title: I to L. Physiotherapy role after diagnosis

items: **Osteoporotic fracture**: pain management, gentle mobility, posture and back extensor strengthening, falls prevention, avoid loaded spinal flexion and twisting early (see Vol 11 Ch 5).
**Metastatic disease**: maintain function within the oncology team plan; avoid manual therapy over affected levels; know the spinal stability status from the medical team.
**Axial spondyloarthritis**: regular mobility and strengthening exercise, aerobic exercise, postural training, alongside medical treatment.
**Pain that wakes the patient but improves on moving in bed is likely?** Mechanical. Constant pain unaffected by position is more concerning.
**Which cancers commonly spread to bone?** Breast, lung, prostate, kidney, thyroid.
**Why measure height?** Height loss can indicate vertebral compression fractures.
**Right shoulder blade pain after fatty meals suggests?** Gallbladder disease.
**A 25-year-old man with morning stiffness for 2 hours that improves with exercise?** Possible axial spondyloarthritis; rheumatology referral.
